model_provenance.why: the model name appears only in task text and in dataset-scope lists such as configs/tiny_recovery_yolo26s_v1.yaml:40 ('D455 hard negatives'); no committed device record (serial number, firmware, rs-enumerate-devices output) exists in this repository
model_provenance.missing_datum: the serial number and firmware version of the unit actually mounted

intrinsics.missing_datum: one committed intrinsics record for the exact depth/colour streams in the exact resolution profile that will be used
intrinsics.would_come_from: on the device: rs-enumerate-devices -c (or pyrealsense2 pipeline.get_active_profile().get_stream(rs.stream.depth).as_video_stream_profile().get_intrinsics()) saved as configs/camera/d455_<serial>_<mode>_intrinsics.json and committed

rejected_substitutes.why: the file header itself says 'ENGINEERING_V0_1 camera rig placeholder (no sensor/render)'. It has no intrinsics and no D455 identity, so it cannot stand in for a calibration; the 0.29 m baseline is rig geometry, not a measured stereo baseline.
an engineered proxy calibration for rendering/synthetic data, explicitly labelled '代理标定'; it is not a measurement of any D455
a long-lens render camera used to draw the size ladder; physically unrelated to a D455
the repository states the gap itself

resolution.missing_datum: the actual stream profile the perception stack runs (D455 supports several; the choice sets the intrinsics, so it cannot be assumed independently of them)
resolution.would_come_from: the same intrinsics record; profile name e.g. 848x480x30 or 1280x720x30

rgb_depth_alignment.missing_datum: whether the pipeline runs align(rs.stream.color) (depth expressed in the colour optical frame) or publishes the raw depth frame, and T_depth_color in the chosen mode
rgb_depth_alignment.would_come_from: the pipeline configuration in code plus depth_profile.get_extrinsics_to(color_profile) on the device
rgb_depth_alignment.why_it_matters: with alignment off, a pixel (u,v) in RGB and the same (u,v) in depth are DIFFERENT rays; every 3D projection in P7 depends on which one is true

frame_rate.missing_datum: the configured sensor frame rate and whether it is the same for depth and colour
frame_rate.would_come_from: the pipeline config plus a timestamp log (P6-06 owns the timing protocol)

depth_units.missing_datum: the depth scale factor of the unit (a per-device value, NOT a constant to hardcode)
depth_units.would_come_from: depth_sensor.get_depth_scale() at connect time, stored alongside the serial number. Assuming 0.001 m would silently put every ball 10x off if the device reports 0.0001.

distortion.missing_datum: the distortion model and coefficients for the colour stream (the D455 RGB stream is typically Brown-Conrady; the VALUES are still per-device)
distortion.would_come_from: the intrinsics record; a factory calibration read from the device is the minimum, a chessboard/charuco re-calibration is the honest maximum

extrinsics_mount_to_camera.missing_datum: T_mount_camera: where the camera sits on the robot and how it is aimed
extrinsics_mount_to_camera.would_come_from: hand-eye calibration (or a measured CAD mount) against the chassis/arm base frame; the FOV of a camera is not a substitute for its pose

robot_mount_frame.convention: REP-103 body frame: +X forward, +Y left, +Z up, right-handed
robot_mount_frame.note: this is the frame the arm and chassis use; the frame tree in frame_tree.json is expressed in it

camera_optical_frame.convention: REP-103 optical frame: +Z forward out of the lens, +X right in the image, +Y down, right-handed

rotation_from_mount_to_optical.derivation: the matrix columns are the mount axes expressed in optical coordinates: X_mount->(0,0,1)=optical +Z, Y_mount->(-1,0,0)=optical -X, Z_mount->(0,-1,0)=optical -Y. The matrix itself is the record; the quaternion is its wxyz encoding.
rotation_from_mount_to_optical.note: the AXES are fixed by the two conventions; the camera's POSE on the robot is a different quantity and stays UNKNOWN above

camera_optical_frame.handedness_check: determinant of the matrix above is +1 (both frames are right-handed)

frames.distinction_rule: camera_optical_frame != robot_mount_frame: they differ by a fixed 90-degree permutation (R_x(-90) then R_z(-90)). A depth point (X,Y,Z)_optical is (Z, -X, -Y) in the mount frame. Mixing them rotates every ball position by 90 degrees and is invisible in a 2D overlay.

derives a 50 mm cube and a mast from the placeholder above; it contains no camera model at all.

repository_sources_checked.content: The repository holds no calibrated fx
repository_sources_checked.why: the project already recorded that any fx in this repo is absent, so filling these fields here would be invention.

verdict.summary: NO D455 field is known from a committed source. What IS proven: the repository's only camera numbers are labelled placeholders, and the optical-vs-mount axis convention is stated exactly.

fill_procedure: 1. On a host with the device attached: rs-enumerate-devices -c > d455_<serial>_<fw>_enumerate.txt

2. pyrealsense2: pick the exact stream profile the perception stack will run; read intrinsics + distortion for colour, intrinsics for depth, depth_sensor.get_depth_scale(), and depth_profile.get_extrinsics_to(color_profile)
3. Write configs/camera/d455_<serial>_<mode>.json with those numbers plus the profile name and firmware
4. Commit it, hash it, and point build_p6_frame_contract.py at it so these fields stop being UNKNOWN
5. Hand-eye calibrate T_mount_camera separately and commit that as its own record - it is a robot measurement, not a camera fact
